name: Move beyond prompt-based personality prompting by training LLMs

representative_ideas: Move beyond prompt-based personality prompting by training LLMs on a large-scale human-grounded dialogue dataset to achieve realistic and valid personality expression.
common_problems: Prompt-based methods for inducing personality in LLMs result in superficial and unrealistic behaviors that fail to capture the nuance of human personality expression and lack psychometric validity.
solution_approaches: Construct a large-scale human-grounded dialogue dataset (BIG5-CHAT) and employ Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to internalize personality traits directly into the model weights.
story: Reframe personality assignment from a 'prompting trick' to a 'data-driven alignment problem,' demonstrating that training on human-grounded data not only improves realism but also uncovers emergent cognitive benefits linking personality to reasoning.
application: Personalized educational tutors, empathetic customer service bots, realistic NPC dialogue generation in gaming.

title: BIG5-CHAT: Shaping LLM Personalities Through Training on Human-Grounded Data

name: Applies diffusion model principles to Chain-of-Thought reasoning to

representative_ideas: Applies diffusion model principles to Chain-of-Thought reasoning to enable iterative correction of intermediate steps and mitigate error accumulation.
common_problems: Standard autoregressive Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning suffers from error accumulation, where early mistakes cannot be corrected and propagate irreversibly through the reasoning chain.
solution_approaches: Reformulate CoT reasoning as an iterative denoising process using a sliding-window mechanism and a causal diffusion noise schedule, allowing the model to retrospectively correct intermediate steps.
story: Elevates reasoning from a linear generation problem to an iterative refinement process, borrowing the 'denoising' metaphor from diffusion models to solve the irreversibility of autoregressive thought chains.
application: Complex mathematical problem solving, multi-step logical deduction, automated planning systems.

title: DiffCoT: Diffusion-styled Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in LLMs

name: Shift from general-purpose LLMs to specialized Large Action

representative_ideas: Shift from general-purpose LLMs to specialized Large Action Models (xLAM) optimized for function calling and action execution to improve agent reliability.
common_problems: General-purpose Large Language Models often struggle with reliable action generation and precise function calling in complex agentic workflows due to their training focus on general text rather than structured actions.
solution_approaches: Introduce a specialized model family (xLAM) trained on curated action-oriented datasets, optimizing the model specifically for planning, tool use, and structured execution instead of conversational fluency.
story: Shift the narrative from 'LLMs as general reasoners' to 'LLMs as specialized action engines,' arguing that the future of agentic AI depends on models explicitly optimized for execution rather than just reasoning.
application: Autonomous tool-use agents, API-calling automation systems, complex workflow orchestration engines.

title: xLAM: A Family of Large Action Models to Empower AI Agent Systems

name: Replaces gradient-based adaptation with a statistical dependency measure

representative_ideas: Replaces gradient-based adaptation with a statistical dependency measure (Brownian Distance Covariance) to achieve efficient, training-free domain adaptation for Vision-Language Models.
common_problems: Vision-language models suffer performance degradation under domain shifts, while existing test-time adaptation methods are computationally intensive, unstable due to back-propagation, or limited to single modalities.
solution_approaches: Propose a training-free method (TaTa) that utilizes Brownian Distance Covariance to capture non-linear dependencies for dynamic adaptation, integrated with attribute-enhanced prompting and pseudo-label refinement.
story: Reconceptualize test-time adaptation from an 'optimization problem' (updating weights) to a 'measurement problem' (statistical dependency), offering a stable, efficient alternative that avoids the risks and costs of back-propagation.
application: Real-time video analysis on edge devices, adaptive medical imaging diagnosis, autonomous driving in changing weather conditions

title: Training-Free Test-Time Adaptation with Brownian Distance Covariance in Vision-Language Models

name: A comprehensive gymnasium suite designed to diagnose and

representative_ideas: A comprehensive gymnasium suite designed to diagnose and improve the integration of perception, memory, and action in Vision-Language Models through controllable, multi-step interactive environments.
common_problems: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are primarily evaluated on static tasks, leaving their ability to integrate perception, memory, and action in multi-step interactive scenarios poorly understood and characterized.
solution_approaches: Introduce VisGym, a suite of 17 environments with flexible controls over difficulty and feedback, paired with multi-step solvers to generate structured demonstrations for supervised finetuning.
story: Reframes VLM evaluation from static perception to 'interactive visual intelligence,' exposing the fragility of frontier models in long-horizon tasks and revealing counter-intuitive failure modes such as the inability to utilize unbounded context effectively.
application: Robotics simulation, interactive game agents, VLM training and evaluation pipelines.

title: VisGym: Diverse, Customizable, Scalable Environments for Multimodal Agents

name: Leverage executable Python code generated by LLMs to

representative_ideas: Leverage executable Python code generated by LLMs to produce verifiable, multi-step reasoning traces for table understanding, creating a high-quality supervision framework.
common_problems: Current multimodal table understanding datasets lack explicit multi-step reasoning supervision, leading to models that produce brief, uninterpretable answers with unverified reasoning paths.
solution_approaches: Develop CoReTab, a framework that couples reasoning steps with executable Python code to verify results; use this to curate a verified dataset and fine-tune MLLMs through a three-stage pipeline to internalize the code-driven reasoning process.
story: Reframe the supervision bottleneck as a 'verifiability' problem, shifting from black-box text generation to 'executable thought' paradigms where reasoning traces are not just readable but runnable and auditable.
application: Automated financial report analysis, scientific table interpretation, complex data extraction from documents.

title: CoReTab: Improving Multimodal Table Understanding with Code-driven Reasoning

name: Constrain dynamics model learning to a latent manifold

representative_ideas: Constrain dynamics model learning to a latent manifold using energy-based models to detect out-of-distribution states and stabilize offline policy optimization.
common_problems: Model-based offline RL suffers from compounding model errors and value overestimation when rollouts deviate from the dataset support (distribution shift), as standard models cannot reliably distinguish in-distribution dynamics from hallucinated ones.
solution_approaches: Propose MC-ETM: train conditional energy-based transition models with a manifold projection-diffusion sampler to generate hard negatives; use the learned energy as a reliability signal to truncate unreliable rollouts and apply pessimistic penalties based on energy-guided sample dispersion.
story: Frame the offline RL reliability problem as a geometric and energetic challenge, defining a 'boundary of reality' via energy landscapes on a learned manifold to strictly separate trustworthy dynamics from extrapolation artifacts.
application: Offline policy training for robotics, autonomous systems from logged data, high-stakes control in healthcare or finance.

title: Manifold-Constrained Energy-Based Transition Models for Offline Reinforcement Learning

name: A comprehensive survey that re-organizes the field of

representative_ideas: A comprehensive survey that re-organizes the field of anomaly and OOD detection by proposing a new taxonomy based on the functional role of Large Language Models.
common_problems: The rapid integration of Large Language Models into anomaly and OOD detection lacks a unified theoretical framework, making it difficult to categorize existing methods, understand the paradigm shift from traditional approaches, and identify future research directions.
solution_approaches: A systematic survey methodology that proposes a novel taxonomy categorizing approaches based on the specific role of the LLM (e.g., as a feature extractor, detector, or generator), followed by a synthesis of challenges and opportunities in this emerging intersection.
story: Position the integration of LLMs as a fundamental paradigm shift in reliability engineering, moving from statistical outlier analysis to semantic comprehension of normality and abnormality. This framing elevates the survey from a mere list of papers to a conceptual roadmap for the field.
application: Industrial monitoring, financial fraud detection, network intrusion detection, medical diagnosis support, log analysis for software reliability.

title: Large Language Models for Anomaly and Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Survey

name: Investigate and quantify the trade-off between task-specific fine-tuning

representative_ideas: Investigate and quantify the trade-off between task-specific fine-tuning and the preservation of intrinsic chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities in LLMs.
common_problems: While fine-tuning is essential for adapting LLMs to specific tasks, its impact on the model's intrinsic chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities remains poorly understood, risking the degradation of core reasoning skills during adaptation.
solution_approaches: Conduct a comprehensive empirical analysis to quantify how different fine-tuning strategies and data compositions affect CoT performance, identifying conditions that preserve or degrade reasoning abilities.
story: Frame fine-tuning not just as a method for knowledge injection but as a potential hazard to reasoning integrity, shifting the focus from 'performance on the target task' to 'preservation of general reasoning faculties.'
application: Robust model adaptation pipelines, development of reasoning-preserving fine-tuning protocols, safety-critical NLP applications.

title: On the Impact of Fine-Tuning on Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

name: Enhances LLM agents by combining Monte Carlo Tree

representative_ideas: Enhances LLM agents by combining Monte Carlo Tree Search with step-level self-critique to generate verified training data for self-improvement.
common_problems: LLM agents produce sub-optimal actions in multi-step tasks, and trajectory-level critiques are too coarse to pinpoint specific erroneous steps for effective correction.
solution_approaches: Propose SLSC-MCTS, which integrates Monte Carlo Tree Search with step-level self-critique, using node values to filter effective critiques and generating high-quality data for iterative self-training.
story: Shifts the narrative from passive agent execution to active 'self-correction via search,' empowering agents to autonomously distinguish useful critiques from noise and bootstrap their own reasoning capabilities.
application: Web shopping agents, multi-hop question answering, automated decision systems.

title: Empowering Large Language Model Agent through Step-Level Self-Critique and Self-Training

name: A multi-agent LLM framework that decomposes next POI

representative_ideas: A multi-agent LLM framework that decomposes next POI prediction into specialized roles (profiling, forecasting, predicting) to handle numeric spatiotemporal data and constrain the prediction space.
common_problems: Directly applying LLMs to next POI prediction fails because LLMs cannot intrinsically understand numeric spatiotemporal patterns and struggle with the vast, unconstrained candidate POI space.
solution_approaches: Propose a collaborative multi-agent framework (CoMaPOI) with three specialized agents: a Profiler to translate numeric data to semantics, a Forecaster to constrain the candidate space, and a Predictor to make the final choice.
story: Reframe the application of LLMs to spatiotemporal tasks from a 'direct prompting' approach to a 'collaborative division of labor,' arguing that complex reasoning requires specialized agents to bridge the modality gap and constrain the solution space.
application: Location-based services, personalized travel recommendation, urban mobility analysis.

title: CoMaPOI: A Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework for Next POI Prediction Bridging the Gap Between Trajectory and Language

name: A granular, component-level analysis of the RARR framework

representative_ideas: A granular, component-level analysis of the RARR framework revealing that the evidence-text agreement module is the primary bottleneck for hallucination mitigation.
common_problems: Hallucination mitigation pipelines like RARR are often treated as monolithic systems, obscuring which specific components (retrieval, agreement, revision) are responsible for performance bottlenecks.
solution_approaches: Conduct a component-level ablation study of the RARR framework using public tools, identifying the agreement module as the weak link through sentence-level granular analysis.
story: Reframes the research contribution from 'building a better system' to 'diagnosing the existing one,' providing a forensic breakdown that isolates the agreement module as the critical failure point in hallucination mitigation.
application: Fact-checking pipelines, automated content verification, system debugging for LLMs.

title: RARR Unraveled: Component-Level Insights into Hallucination Detection and Mitigation

name: Achieve efficient test-time adaptation for VLMs by rotating

representative_ideas: Achieve efficient test-time adaptation for VLMs by rotating the feature space basis to amplify class distinctions without requiring model updates.
common_problems: Existing test-time adaptation methods for Vision-Language Models are either computationally expensive due to backpropagation or ineffective because they operate within the constraints of the original, potentially suboptimal feature space.
solution_approaches: Propose a training-free framework that reconstructs the feature space via basis transformation (space rotation) to maximize inter-class distinctions, supplemented by a dynamic queue to maintain representative sample prototypes during inference.
story: Reframe test-time adaptation from a model parameter updating problem into a geometric feature alignment problem, demonstrating that rotating the feature basis without gradient computation can outperform heavy optimization methods.
application: Real-time adaptive vision systems, edge-device deployment where backpropagation is infeasible, rapid domain adaptation for robotics vision.

title: Space Rotation with Basis Transformation for Training-free Test-Time Adaptation

name: Replace complex Chain-of-Thought reasoning with a simpler Chain-of-Rank

representative_ideas: Replace complex Chain-of-Thought reasoning with a simpler Chain-of-Rank approach for domain-specific RAG, enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
common_problems: Small-scale LLMs on edge devices struggle with the computational cost and learning difficulty of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning required for domain-specific RAG applications.
solution_approaches: Propose Chain-of-Rank (CoR), which replaces generative reasoning steps with a simpler task of ranking the reliability of retrieved documents, reducing computational overhead while preserving accuracy.
story: Reframe the reasoning requirement in RAG from 'generating explanations' to 'assessing reliability,' arguing that for specialized edge AI, discriminative ranking is a sufficient and more efficient proxy for complex reasoning.
application: On-device personal assistants, mobile enterprise search, privacy-preserving local RAG systems.

title: Chain-of-Rank: Enhancing Large Language Models for Domain-Specific RAG in Edge Device

name: Improve LLM agent robustness by identifying suboptimal actions

representative_ideas: Improve LLM agent robustness by identifying suboptimal actions during exploration and training on LLM-generated 'calibrated' trajectories that correct these mistakes.
common_problems: LLM agents often fail in long-horizon tasks because suboptimal actions accumulate and cause the agent to drift from the correct trajectory, and existing learning methods lack a mechanism to correct these intermediate errors.
solution_approaches: Propose STeCa, a framework that detects suboptimal steps via reward comparison, uses LLM reflection to generate 'calibrated trajectories' that correct these steps in hindsight, and trains the agent on this refined data to enforce robust decision-making.
story: Elevate agent learning from simple imitation or binary preference to 'process-level calibration'; the narrative frames failure not as a dead-end but as a resource for generating counterfactual success, teaching agents how to recover from errors rather than just avoiding them.
application: Autonomous web navigation, complex workflow automation, robotic task planning

title: STeCa: Step-level Trajectory Calibration for LLM Agent Learning

name: Formalizes 'Metaphysical Reasoning' as a three-step discriminative process

representative_ideas: Formalizes 'Metaphysical Reasoning' as a three-step discriminative process to evaluate LLMs' ability to comprehend situational changes, a critical missing piece for developing conscious agents.
common_problems: LLMs lack the ability to comprehend situational changes (transitions) triggered by environmental factors or actions, limiting their utility as reliable autonomous agents in dynamic environments.
solution_approaches: Formulate reasoning under distributional changes as a three-step discriminative process (action plausibility, state changes, situational transitions) and construct a multi-task benchmark (MARS) to systematically assess these capabilities.
story: Elevate the engineering challenge of tracking state changes into 'Metaphysical Reasoning,' positioning it as a fundamental prerequisite for generalizable agency and consciousness, thereby defining a new frontier beyond static knowledge benchmarks.
application: Autonomous agents in dynamic environments, robotics planning, interactive storytelling, simulation environments

title: MARS: Benchmarking the Metaphysical Reasoning Abilities of Language Models with a Multi-task Evaluation Dataset

name: Achieve state-of-the-art automated theorem proving with smaller models

representative_ideas: Achieve state-of-the-art automated theorem proving with smaller models by combining scaffolded synthetic curriculum learning, compiler-guided self-correction, and model averaging to overcome data scarcity and diversity loss.
common_problems: Automated theorem provers struggle to generalize to complex theorems due to scarce training data, and suffer from training instability where model diversity collapses in later stages, limiting the discovery of novel proofs.
solution_approaches: A training pipeline featuring scaffolded data synthesis to generate a curriculum of increasingly difficult problems, verifier-guided self-correction allowing the model to iteratively refine proofs using compiler feedback, and model averaging to preserve output diversity.
story: Reframe theorem proving from a static generation task into an interactive, curriculum-driven self-improvement process. By treating the proof assistant as an external verifier for self-correction and synthesizing a 'curriculum' of problems, the work demonstrates that efficient training dynamics and inference-time compute strategies can outperform raw model scaling.
application: Formal verification of software systems, mathematical research assistance, automated code generation and repair, intelligent tutoring systems for logic.

title: Goedel-Prover-V2: Scaling Formal Theorem Proving with Scaffolded Data Synthesis and Self-Correction

name: Bridge the performance gap between full-precision and low-bit

representative_ideas: Bridge the performance gap between full-precision and low-bit models by initiating training in 16-bit and transitioning to 1.58-bit quantization-aware training at an optimal point.
common_problems: Training low-bit LLMs (e.g., 1.58-bit) from scratch often yields suboptimal performance compared to full-precision models, while post-training quantization suffers from accuracy degradation.
solution_approaches: Propose a continual quantization-aware pre-training strategy: start with standard 16-bit pre-training, then transition to 1.58-bit quantization-aware training; utilize techniques like optimizer state retention and gradual quantization phasing to mitigate loss spikes during the transition.
story: Reframe quantization not as a post-hoc compression step or a scratch-only constraint, but as a 'developmental stage' in the training lifecycle, investigating the optimal 'growth spurt' moment to transition a model from high-precision plasticity to low-bit efficiency.
application: Training efficient LLMs for edge deployment, optimizing foundation model training costs, sustainable AI development.

title: Continual Quantization-Aware Pre-Training: When to transition from 16-bit to 1.58-bit pre-training for BitNet language models?

name: Reformulates zero-shot action recognition as a retrieval process

representative_ideas: Reformulates zero-shot action recognition as a retrieval process over a structured cache, using LLMs to semantically weight visual descriptors for training-free adaptation.
common_problems: Skeleton-based zero-shot action recognition models struggle to generalize to unseen actions during inference, and standard adaptation techniques require unavailable training data or back-propagation.
solution_approaches: Introduce a non-parametric cache storing structured global and local skeleton descriptors and reformulate inference as a retrieval process, using LLMs to assign semantic importance weights for fusing predictions.
story: Elevate the inference process by integrating an LLM as a 'semantic brain' to guide the fusion of visual features, framing test-time adaptation as a retrieval-and-reasoning synergy rather than model fine-tuning.
application: Surveillance systems recognizing novel actions, human-robot interaction, sports analytics for new movement types

title: Boosting Skeleton-based Zero-Shot Action Recognition with Training-Free Test-Time Adaptation

name: Replace standard inner products with quantum-inspired high-order tensor

representative_ideas: Replace standard inner products with quantum-inspired high-order tensor products to enhance representation expressiveness without altering model architecture or increasing parameters.
common_problems: Improving LLM performance typically requires costly architectural redesigns or increased parameter counts, while standard multiplicative operations (inner product) limit the expressiveness of existing representations.
solution_approaches: Develop a quantum-inspired high-order product operation that re-parameterizes vectors/matrices into high-dimensional Hilbert space forms; integrate this as a transparent, in-place replacement for standard operations in Transformers (embeddings, attention, MLP) without adding parameters.
story: Shift the innovation focus from macro-level architecture engineering to micro-level atomic operations, framing the method as a 'fundamental reinvention' of the building blocks of deep learning that is orthogonal and compatible with existing architectural advances.
application: Enhancing pre-trained LLMs via efficient fine-tuning, upgrading model capacity in resource-constrained environments, plug-and-play performance boosts for legacy architectures.

title: Reinvent the Operation not the Architecture: Quantum-inspired High-order Product for Compatible and Improved LLMs Training

name: Enhance language models' spatial reasoning capabilities by integrating

representative_ideas: Enhance language models' spatial reasoning capabilities by integrating spatial logical rules as constraints during training to enforce correct abstraction and generalization.
common_problems: State-of-the-art language models fail at complex spatial reasoning, particularly with nested expressions, because they lack the necessary level of abstraction to generalize beyond surface-level patterns.
solution_approaches: Integrate neuro-symbolic training where spatial logical rules act as constraints, providing auxiliary supervision that forces the model to learn structural abstractions rather than just statistical correlations.
story: Reframe spatial reasoning failures as a lack of structural abstraction, proposing that injecting symbolic logic acts as a 'cognitive scaffold' that guides the model to internalize the rules of space rather than merely mimicking spatial language.
application: Robotics navigation instructions, indoor layout design assistants, geographic information systems (GIS) query interfaces.

title: Neuro-symbolic Training for Reasoning over Spatial Language

name: Introduce a dataset (A3CG) that links sustainability aspects

representative_ideas: Introduce a dataset (A3CG) that links sustainability aspects to verifiable actions to immunize NLP-based ESG analysis against greenwashing and ensure robustness against shifting reporting strategies.
common_problems: Existing NLP methods for ESG analysis lack robustness against greenwashing, often extracting misleading or exaggerated sustainability claims as if they were objective performance indicators.
solution_approaches: Construct a dataset (A3CG) that enforces fine-grained linking between sustainability aspects and specific actions, and train models to generalize across categories to handle selective reporting.
story: Reframe ESG analysis from a standard information extraction task to a trustworthiness and verification challenge, arguing that true insight requires grounding abstract claims in verifiable actions to combat strategic deception.
application: Automated ESG auditing tools, sustainable investment risk assessment, regulatory compliance monitoring.

title: Towards Robust ESG Analysis Against Greenwashing Risks: Aspect-Action Analysis with Cross-Category Generalization

name: A specialized, efficient on-device language model designed specifically

representative_ideas: A specialized, efficient on-device language model designed specifically for accurate and low-latency software API function calling.
common_problems: General-purpose Large Language Models are computationally expensive and often impractical for on-device execution, while smaller models struggle with the precision required for accurate software API function calling.
solution_approaches: Develop 'Octopus', a compact language model specifically trained and optimized for the function calling domain, enabling it to run locally on devices while maintaining high accuracy in mapping natural language instructions to API calls.
story: Shift the narrative from general-purpose cloud intelligence to specialized, privacy-preserving edge intelligence; the work positions the LLM not as a chatbot but as a native operating system interface that bridges user intent and software capability without network dependency.
application: Mobile OS assistants, IoT device control, privacy-first automation tools

title: Octopus: On-device language model for function calling of software APIs

name: A training-free strategy to improve Concept Bottleneck Models

representative_ideas: A training-free strategy to improve Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) in new domains by surgically masking confounding concepts and amplifying discriminative ones using minimal image-level labels.
common_problems: Explainable medical image classifiers (CBMs) suffer performance drops in new clinical environments due to concept-level shifts, and fine-tuning risks degrading concept faithfulness while requiring expensive expert annotations.
solution_approaches: Develop a training-free strategy that uses minimal image-level labels to identify confounding concepts (to mask) and discriminative concepts (to amplify), dynamically adjusting the inference pathway without updating weights.
story: Frame the adaptation of explainable models as a 'concept debugging' process rather than model retraining, arguing that preserving the semantic integrity of concepts while surgically adjusting their influence is key to trustworthy deployment.
application: Deploying diagnostic tools across different hospitals, adapting histopathology models to new staining protocols

title: Training-free Test-time Improvement for Explainable Medical Image Classification

name: Improve cross-document coreference by synthetically reconstructing the missing

representative_ideas: Improve cross-document coreference by synthetically reconstructing the missing discourse context between mentions to bridge the information gap.
common_problems: Cross-document coreference resolution suffers from a lack of contextual coherence between mentions, as they are scattered across different documents, unlike within-document scenarios where rich context links entities and events.
solution_approaches: Introduce a Cross-Document Discourse Coherence Enhancement (CD-DCE) task that retrieves and inserts coherent text between two cross-document mentions to form a pseudo-coherent document, enabling better representation learning for coreference resolution.
story: Reframe the cross-document context gap as a 'missing discourse' problem rather than an information retrieval limit; by synthetically reconstructing coherence, the work allows models to apply intra-document reasoning capabilities to inter-document tasks.
application: Multi-document summarization, knowledge graph construction, intelligence analysis

title: Employing Discourse Coherence Enhancement to Improve Cross-Document Event and Entity Coreference Resolution

name: A novel benchmark designed to evaluate the capability

representative_ideas: A novel benchmark designed to evaluate the capability of models to discover and reason about abstract causal events beyond surface-level textual cues.
common_problems: Existing causal reasoning benchmarks focus primarily on concrete, explicit events, failing to assess the model's ability to understand abstract causal relationships necessary for high-level cognitive tasks.
solution_approaches: Construct the ACCESS benchmark, providing a specialized dataset and evaluation protocols that require models to identify and reason about causal links between abstract events, moving beyond literal text matching.
story: Reframe causal reasoning evaluation from recognizing explicit linguistic patterns to mastering cognitive abstraction; the work argues that true intelligence requires detaching from concrete entities to reason about generalized event structures.
application: Policy impact analysis, strategic planning systems, advanced narrative understanding

title: ACCESS : A Benchmark for Abstract Causal Event Discovery and Reasoning

name: Augment multi-step RAG with a hypergraph-structured memory that

representative_ideas: Augment multi-step RAG with a hypergraph-structured memory that actively synthesizes high-order correlations among facts to guide reasoning, moving beyond passive fact storage.
common_problems: Existing RAG memory modules act as passive storage for isolated facts, failing to capture high-order correlations and complex relationships required for global sense-making and deep reasoning in long contexts.
solution_approaches: Introduce HGMem, a hypergraph-based memory mechanism where hyperedges represent memory units to model high-order interactions; this structure evolves during reasoning to connect facts and thoughts into an integrated knowledge structure that guides subsequent steps.
story: Elevate the concept of 'memory' in AI systems from a static warehouse of facts to a dynamic 'reasoning engine' that actively structures knowledge, arguing that intelligence lies in the connectivity between facts rather than the facts themselves.
application: Complex question answering, long-horizon investigative analysis, knowledge management systems, multi-hop reasoning tasks.

title: Improving Multi-step RAG with Hypergraph-based Memory for Long-Context Complex Relational Modeling

name: Demonstrates that specific prompt formulations significantly enhance the

representative_ideas: Demonstrates that specific prompt formulations significantly enhance the ability of LLMs to retrieve and quote verbatim text from their pre-training corpus.
common_problems: LLMs often struggle to reliably quote or retrieve specific knowledge from their pre-training data when prompted generically, making it difficult to distinguish between hallucination and memorization.
solution_approaches: Investigate and design specific prompting strategies, such as 'According to...' prefixes, that trigger verbatim retrieval behaviors and allow for systematic study of memorization.
story: Frames quoting not merely as a retrieval task but as a prompt-sensitivity phenomenon, linking prompting strategies directly to the activation of latent training data and raising implications for data attribution and privacy.
application: Copyright auditing, training data extraction, analyzing model hallucinations vs. memorization.

title: “According to . . . ”: Prompting Language Models Improves Quoting from Pre-Training Data

name: Identify critical limitations in current vector-database-based long-term memory

representative_ideas: Identify critical limitations in current vector-database-based long-term memory for agents and propose a research agenda centered on cognitive-inspired memory differentiation and management.
common_problems: Current LLM agents rely on monolithic vector database implementations for long-term memory, failing to differentiate between cognitive memory types (e.g., procedural vs. semantic) or manage memory evolution over an agent's lifetime.
solution_approaches: A conceptual framework that advocates for separating memory types using metadata and integrating external knowledge sources, moving beyond simple vector retrieval to structured, lifetime-aware memory management.
story: Elevate the engineering discussion of 'memory storage' into a research agenda for 'cognitive architecture,' arguing that robust agent autonomy requires moving beyond retrieval to human-like memory organization.
application: Long-term personal AI assistants, autonomous robots with lifelong learning capabilities, complex multi-session dialogue systems.

title: Memory Matters: The Need to Improve Long-Term Memory in LLM-Agents

name: LLMs exhibit amplified belief congruence (group identity bias)

representative_ideas: LLMs exhibit amplified belief congruence (group identity bias) compared to humans, harming simulation fidelity, but social psychology-inspired interventions can mitigate this.
common_problems: When used in multi-agent societal simulations, LLMs exhibit 'belief congruence' (preference for similar identities) more intensely than humans, leading to echo chambers, increased misinformation spread, and impaired learning.
solution_approaches: Develop a multi-agent framework to quantify this bias and introduce intervention strategies derived from social psychology—contact hypothesis, accuracy nudges, and global citizenship framing—to align agent behavior with pro-social norms.
story: Bridge social psychology and AI alignment by diagnosing LLMs with 'social pathologies' (excessive tribalism) and importing established human social theories as therapeutic interventions, reframing alignment as a group-dynamics problem rather than an individual instruction-following problem.
application: Social dynamics simulation, bias auditing in generative agents, collaborative AI systems

title: Mind the (Belief) Gap: Group Identity in the World of LLMs

name: Improve zeroth-order optimization for LLM fine-tuning by adapting

representative_ideas: Improve zeroth-order optimization for LLM fine-tuning by adapting the perturbation sampling strategy using momentum and uncertainty, rather than relying on standard gradient momentum.
common_problems: Zeroth-order optimization methods (like MeZO) for LLM fine-tuning suffer from severe oscillations, slow convergence, and overfitting due to random perturbation sampling and ineffective momentum utilization.
solution_approaches: Propose ZO-AdaMU, which integrates momentum and uncertainty directly into the perturbation generation process of the stochastic approximation, stabilizing the gradient estimation step.
story: Reframe the role of momentum in zeroth-order learning from a gradient smoothing technique to a mechanism for guiding the search direction (perturbation), transforming a memory-efficient hack into a theoretically sound and robust optimization paradigm.
application: On-device LLM fine-tuning, resource-constrained model training, black-box model adaptation.

title: ZO-AdaMU Optimizer: Adapting Perturbation by the Momentum and Uncertainty in Zeroth-Order Optimization

name: A physics-informed transformer architecture that couples multi-scale deterministic

representative_ideas: A physics-informed transformer architecture that couples multi-scale deterministic evolution with stochastic generation, enforcing physical constraints directly into the loss function for accurate extreme weather nowcasting.
common_problems: Deep learning models for precipitation nowcasting struggle with the chaotic, multi-scale dynamics of storms and lack physical consistency, resulting in blurry forecasts and unreliable predictions for extreme events.
solution_approaches: A hybrid architecture combining a deterministic Evolution Network (with Scale-Aware Temporal Residual Modulation) and a stochastic Generative Network (with spatio-temporal adapters), trained via a Multi-scale Physics-informed Loss that enforces physical constraints and uncertainty calibration.
story: Elevate weather nowcasting from a pure sequence prediction task to a physics-constrained simulation problem. By embedding physical laws directly into the transformer architecture and loss function, the work bridges the gap between data-driven flexibility and physical fidelity, offering a new paradigm for reliable disaster prediction.
application: Smart city disaster warning systems, flood risk assessment, aviation weather monitoring, short-term severe weather alerts.

title: Multi-scale Physics-informed Transformer With Spatio-temporal Feature Adapter For Extreme Precipitation Nowcasting

name: Challenges the 'color-blind' fairness paradigm by introducing 'difference

representative_ideas: Challenges the 'color-blind' fairness paradigm by introducing 'difference awareness,' arguing that context-sensitive group differentiation is necessary for true fairness in specific scenarios.
common_problems: Conventional fairness definitions enforce 'difference unawareness' (color-blindness), which fails in real-world scenarios where contextually appropriate group differentiation is legally required or morally necessary to assess harm correctly.
solution_approaches: Introduce a benchmark suite that distinguishes between descriptive, normative, and correlation-based scenarios, enabling the evaluation of when and how models should exhibit 'difference awareness' rather than blind equality.
story: Reframe the fairness narrative from 'treating everyone the same' to 'treating people appropriately based on context,' challenging the mathematical convenience of color-blindness and establishing 'difference awareness' as a distinct, necessary dimension of ethical AI.
application: Context-aware content moderation, legal reasoning assistants, culturally sensitive dialogue systems, harm assessment tools

title: Fairness through Difference Awareness: Measuring Desired Group Discrimination in LLMs

name: Improve the robustness and calibration of small language

representative_ideas: Improve the robustness and calibration of small language models by augmenting their training data with diverse, LLM-generated counterfactual instances.
common_problems: Small Language Models (SLMs) are efficient but brittle, suffering from poor performance on out-of-domain (OOD) inputs and unreliable confidence estimates (calibration), limiting their deployment in high-stakes scenarios.
solution_approaches: A data augmentation framework where Large Language Models generate minimally altered counterfactual instances to expand the training distribution, combined with rationale-augmented calibration training to transfer robustness from the teacher to the student model.
story: Reframe data augmentation as a 'reasoning transfer' mechanism. Instead of simply scaling up model size, the work scales up the 'experience' of the model through counterfactual reasoning, allowing efficient SLMs to inherit the robustness and calibration properties of large frontier models.
application: Deploying robust QA systems on edge devices, low-resource environments, customer service bots requiring high reliability, mobile assistants.

title: CATfOOD: Counterfactual Augmented Training for Improving Out-of-Domain Performance and Calibration
